records.text: Ample is the glory stored for Olympian winners: thereof my shepherd tongue is fain to keep some part in fold.
records.speaker: Pindar

source.title: The Extant Odes of Pindar
source.attribution: Pindar; English translation by Ernest Myers, The Extant Odes of Pindar (1904). Original text preserved; public domain in the US, Canada and UK. Original Gutenberg producer credits and notices: LICENSES/.

records.text: Now he that hath lately won glory in the time of his sweet youth is lifted on the wings of his strong hope and soaring valour, for his thoughts are above riches.
records.speaker: Pindar

source.title: The Extant Odes of Pindar
source.attribution: Pindar; English translation by Ernest Myers, The Extant Odes of Pindar (1904). Original text preserved; public domain in the US, Canada and UK. Original Gutenberg producer credits and notices: LICENSES/.

records.text: For speech is longer-lived than act, whensoever by favour of the Graces the tongue hath drawn it forth out of the depth of the heart.
records.speaker: Pindar

source.title: The Extant Odes of Pindar
source.attribution: Pindar; English translation by Ernest Myers, The Extant Odes of Pindar (1904). Original text preserved; public domain in the US, Canada and UK. Original Gutenberg producer credits and notices: LICENSES/.

records.text: But when through his labour one fareth well, then are due honey-voiced songs, be they even a prelude to words that shall come after, a pledge confirmed by oath in honour of high excellence.
records.speaker: Pindar

records.text: The quarter is, under the captain, the director of the game.
records.speaker: Walter Camp

source.title: American Football
source.attribution: Walter Camp, American Football (1891). Original text preserved; public domain in the US, Canada and UK. Original Gutenberg producer credits and notices: LICENSES/.
source.section: The Quarter-back

records.text: Every player upon a team has to labor under two distinctly different sets of circumstances: one set arising from the possession of the ball by his opponents, and the other from the possession of the ball by his own side.
records.speaker: Walter Camp

source.title: American Football
source.attribution: Walter Camp, American Football (1891). Original text preserved; public domain in the US, Canada and UK. Original Gutenberg producer credits and notices: LICENSES/.
source.section: End Rusher

records.text: But weight must be given work to do, and that work demands practice, and slowness of execution cannot be tolerated.
records.speaker: Walter Camp

source.title: American Football
source.attribution: Walter Camp, American Football (1891). Original text preserved; public domain in the US, Canada and UK. Original Gutenberg producer credits and notices: LICENSES/.
source.section: The Guard

records.text: A quarter can slow up in a game if advisable, but he can never do any faster work than that which he does in practice without throwing his men completely out.
records.speaker: Walter Camp

source.title: American Football
source.attribution: Walter Camp, American Football (1891). Original text preserved; public domain in the US, Canada and UK. Original Gutenberg producer credits and notices: LICENSES/.
source.section: The Quarter-back

records.text: No matter whether the ball be caught or fumbled, he is then ready to lend assistance; whereas if he stand still after his pass, he is of no use to the rest of the play.
records.speaker: Walter Camp

source.title: American Football
source.attribution: Walter Camp, American Football (1891). Original text preserved; public domain in the US, Canada and UK. Original Gutenberg producer credits and notices: LICENSES/.
source.section: The Quarter-back

records.text: The coach can choose no more helpful course during the first few days, as far as the quarter is concerned, than that of persuading him to repose confidence in his men.
records.speaker: Walter Camp

source.title: American Football
source.attribution: Walter Camp, American Football (1891). Original text preserved; public domain in the US, Canada and UK. Original Gutenberg producer credits and notices: LICENSES/.
source.section: The Quarter-back

records.text: He should always believe that the play will be a success.
records.speaker: Walter Camp

source.title: American Football
source.attribution: Walter Camp, American Football (1891). Original text preserved; public domain in the US, Canada and UK. Original Gutenberg producer credits and notices: LICENSES/.
source.section: The Quarter-back

records.text: In practice, great stress should be laid on quick handling and sharp passing of the ball.
records.speaker: Walter Camp

source.title: American Football
source.attribution: Walter Camp, American Football (1891). Original text preserved; public domain in the US, Canada and UK. Original Gutenberg producer credits and notices: LICENSES/.
source.section: The Quarter-back

records.text: Good form is simply the making of the stroke in the best way, so as to get the greatest effect with the least exertion.
records.speaker: James Dwight

source.title: Lawn-tennis
source.attribution: James Dwight, Lawn-tennis (1886). Original text preserved; public domain in the US, Canada and UK. Original Gutenberg producer credits and notices: LICENSES/.
source.section: Part I, Chapter I: How to Learn to Play

records.text: It is of the greatest importance not to handicap yourself at the start by acquiring bad form.
records.speaker: James Dwight

source.title: Lawn-tennis
source.attribution: James Dwight, Lawn-tennis (1886). Original text preserved; public domain in the US, Canada and UK. Original Gutenberg producer credits and notices: LICENSES/.
source.section: Part I, Chapter I: How to Learn to Play

records.text: Always stick to some definite plan, as in that way you get practice in placing.
records.speaker: James Dwight

source.title: Lawn-tennis
source.attribution: James Dwight, Lawn-tennis (1886). Original text preserved; public domain in the US, Canada and UK. Original Gutenberg producer credits and notices: LICENSES/.
source.section: Part I, Chapter I: How to Learn to Play

records.speaker: James Dwight

source.title: Lawn-tennis
